recognize_zh: 高倍視野中同時可見 4–5 顆大型巨核細胞，細胞質豐富、核分葉且形態大致正常，周圍為紅血球系與顆粒球系前驅細胞，呈現 ITP 骨髓常見的巨核細胞增加。
features: Several (4-5) large megakaryocytes in a single high-power field, indicating increased megakaryocyte number
Megakaryocytes have abundant granular eosinophilic cytoplasm and lobulated nuclei without severe atypia
Occasional megakaryocytes with less lobulated or more condensed nuclei, possibly immature forms
Background of maturing erythroid precursors (small round dark nuclei) and granulocytic cells
Loose, somewhat disrupted stroma with processing artifact; focus is limited at the edges
describe_en: High-power view of the bone marrow biopsy shows increased megakaryocytes, with four to five large forms present in one field. They have abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm and lobulated nuclei without significant dysplastic features, and are admixed with maturing erythroid and granulocytic precursors. No fibrosis or abnormal infiltrate is appreciated, although section artifact and focus limit fine detail. In a thrombocytopenic patient, findings are consistent with increased marrow megakaryopoiesis secondary to peripheral platelet destruction, as in immune thrombocytopenia (ITP).

ddx.vs: MPN megakaryocytes form clusters and show hyperlobated (ET) or bulbous, hyperchromatic cloud-like nuclei (PMF) with reticulin fibrosis, and platelet counts are typically high.
Dysplastic megakaryocytes are micromegakaryocytes or hypolobated/separated-lobe forms, unlike the well-lobulated forms here.
Marrow megakaryocytes may also be increased; the peripheral smear (schistocytes) and coagulation or ADAMTS13 studies separate them, not marrow morphology.
